skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components as videos through inference.sh, with configurable dimensions, frame rate, duration, codec, composition, and props.
skill.summary: Turn Remotion TSX animations into remotely rendered video outputs.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting or documentation links, not shell execution or unauthorized network activity. Unpinned skill installation commands create supply-chain exposure, and submitted code and props are processed by inference.sh.

remediation.issue: Installation examples use unpinned remote skill references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each skill dependency to a reviewed immutable version or commit, and document the expected publisher and integrity checks.

remediation.issue: Code and props are sent to an external rendering service.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear data-handling warning and instruct users to remove secrets, credentials, and confidential content before rendering.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.

content.value_statement: Creating polished video from React animation code requires a reliable rendering workflow. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns a rendered video.
actual_capabilities: Renders default-exported React TSX components through the infsh/remotion-render application.
Configures width, height, frame rate, duration, codec, composition identifier, and component props.
Uses documented React and Remotion imports for frame-based animation.
Supports belt CLI and Python SDK requests with optional streaming progress.
Returns a video output reference after remote rendering completes.
limitations: Requires belt CLI login or the inference.sh Python SDK and network access.
Rendering occurs on inference.sh, so submitted code and props leave the local environment.
Available component imports are limited to the documented React and Remotion packages.
The skill provides instructions and examples, not a bundled local renderer.

use_cases.title: Build Product Animations
use_cases.description: Convert a React animation concept into a configured Remotion render for product demos or release clips.

use_cases.title: Produce Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render timed text, counters, sequences, and spring animations at a chosen aspect ratio and frame rate.

use_cases.title: Generate Data-Driven Videos
use_cases.description: Pass structured props into reusable components and monitor longer renders through streamed progress updates.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Title
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-second Remotion title animation with a dark background, white text, 1920x1080 resolution, and 30 FPS. Render it through inference.sh.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner render with basic timing and dimensions

prompt_templates.title: Animate Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Remotion component that accepts title and subtitle props. Fade both elements in, then render a five-second square video.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reusable animation driven by input props

prompt_templates.title: Sequence Multiple Scenes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three timed Remotion scenes using Sequence and interpolate. Configure clean transitions, 60 FPS, and a ten-second duration.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Streaming Render Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Python SDK workflow for a parameterized Remotion component. Include validation, render settings, streamed progress handling, and final video output reporting.

output_examples.input: Render a three-second fade-in title at 1920x1080 and 30 FPS.
output_examples.output: A remote render request is prepared with the title animation, requested dimensions, frame rate, and duration. The completed response identifies the video output.

output_examples.input: Create a square animated counter that reaches 100 percent in five seconds.
output: A 1080x1080 composition uses the current frame to calculate progress.
The render runs for five seconds at the selected frame rate.
The result reports the generated video location.

output_examples.input: Stream progress for a ten-second video created through the Python SDK.
output_examples.output: The workflow reports rendering progress as updates arrive, then presents the final video reference when the service completes processing.

best_practices: Keep animation timing derived from the current frame and configured frame rate.
Test short, low-resolution renders before requesting long or high-resolution output.
Remove secrets and confidential values from code and props before remote submission.
anti_patterns: Do not embed credentials, private URLs, or sensitive customer data in submitted components.
Do not assume browser-only dependencies are available beyond the documented imports.
Do not request expensive final settings before validating composition timing and layout.

faq.question: What input does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires TSX code that default-exports a React component. You may also provide props and render settings.

faq.question: Which Remotion APIs can I use?
faq.answer: The documentation lists frame hooks, interpolation, springs, fills, sequences, audio, video, and image components.

faq.question: Can I control video dimensions and timing?
faq.answer: Yes. You can set width, height, frame rate, duration, codec, and composition identifier.

faq.question: Does rendering happen locally?
faq.answer: No. The examples submit the component and settings to the inference.sh rendering application.

faq.question: Can I monitor render progress?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python SDK example enables streaming and reads progress updates before receiving the final output.

faq.question: Does this skill install its dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents separate installation commands for the belt CLI and related skills.
